name: unicode-and-newline-paths
why: The paths that break a line-oriented reader and a locale-aware sort at once. A newline, a tab, a quote, a space and a literal backslash all have to survive NUL parsing byte for byte. The two `z/` entries are the ordering case that matters: U+1F600 is the surrogate pair D83D DE00, so its first code unit sorts *below* the fullwidth U+FF26, while its UTF-8 bytes sort above them. A digest built on a code-point sort or on UTF-8 byte order disagrees with this golden; UTF-16 code-unit order — the ECMAScript relational operator — is what Athena computed and therefore what the token means.
